title: People Ops: Hiring, Onboarding, Performance & Manager Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's end-to-end people operations practices for hiring, new-employee onboarding, performance & feedback cycles, and manager responsibilities. It is intended for hiring managers, interviewers, people-ops partners, and new managers. Follow the processes below to ensure a consistent candidate experience, reduce time-to-hire, accelerate new-hire time-to-value, and run fair, documentation-driven performance cycles.

Contents
1. Hiring process summary
2. Interview stages & scorecards
3. Offer approvals & compensation guardrails
4. Candidate experience SLAs and metrics
5. New hire onboarding checklist (first 90 days)
6. Performance & feedback cadence
7. Manager responsibilities & templates
8. Systems, tooling, and ownership

1) Hiring process summary

Short intro: We use a structured, hiring-manager-led model supported by People Ops and Recruiting. Recruiting operates the Greenhouse ATS; managers define role requirements and lead hiring decisions. People Ops owns compensation banding, offer approvals, and onboarding policies.

High-level steps (numbered):
1. Requisition approval: Hiring manager opens a req in Greenhouse and attaches an approved role brief and hiring rubric. People Ops reviews for headcount and band alignment.
2. Sourcing & screening: Recruiting sources candidates (internal referrals encouraged) and completes an initial screen.
3. Interview loop: Manager-run loop with standardized scorecard and diversity-aware interviewing practices.
4. Debrief & decision: Interviewers submit scorecards before debrief; hiring manager runs structured debrief.
5. Offer & negotiation: People Ops drafts offer using band guidance; manager approves. Recruiting extends offer and closes the loop.
6. Pre-boarding: New hire paperwork via Rippling; manager receives pre-boarding checklist.
7. Day 0-90 onboarding & 30/60/90 check-ins.

2) Interview stages & scorecards

Standard interview stages (apply these unless the role has an approved deviation):
- Phone screen (Recruiter) — culture fit, role fit, compensation expectations
- Technical screen (IC or manager) — core competency assessment (coding/architecture)
- Work-sample or take-home (if required) — 48–72 hour turnaround recommended
- Onsite/Loop (virtual or in-person) — 4–5 interviews covering: depth of role skills, system design, collaboration & communication, product judgment, and leadership/ownership (for senior roles)

Scorecard fields (required on every role):
- Technical competency: 1–5
- Problem solving: 1–5
- Communication & collaboration: 1–5
- Role-specific skills (1–3 measured attributes): 1–5 each
- Cultural add / values alignment: 1–5
- Overall recommendation: hire / maybe / pass

Debrief guidance (for hiring managers):
- Require completed scorecards before the debrief.
- Use a 15–30 minute structured debrief with the top interviewer(s).
- Document the rationale for hire vs no-hire in the Greenhouse hiring note.

3) Offer approvals & compensation guardrails

Offer flow (numbered):
1. Manager completes approval form in Greenhouse with suggested base and equity.
2. People Ops verifies band, comp philosophy, and budget. If compensation exceeds band midpoint by >10%, exec approval required.
3. Recruiting prepares and extends offer, including benefits summary and expected start date.
4. Negotiation handled by Recruiting + People Ops; final approvals recorded in the offer worksheet.

Quick compensation rules:
- Use published band ranges stored in the People Ops Confluence page.
- Target offers at or below band midpoint for IC hires unless exceptional.
- For senior/critical hires, include a business justification note and required approval chain.

Offer SLA targets:
- Time from final interview to written offer: median 72 hours
- Offer acceptance window: standard 5 business days (exception handled by People Ops)

4) Candidate experience SLAs & metrics

Primary metrics we track (People Ops & Recruiting dashboards):
- Time-to-fill (req open -> accepted): target median 30 days
- Time-to-offer (final interview -> offer): target median 3 days
- Offer acceptance rate: target >= 80%
- Drop-off at phone screen: target < 40%

Communication SLAs:
- Acknowledge incoming applications within 3 business days.
- Schedule first interview (phone screen) within 7 calendar days of initial positive screening.
- Provide interview feedback to candidates within 5 business days post-loop when feasible.

Candidate experience rules:
- Send interview loop agenda and interviewer names at least 48 hours in advance.
- Offer virtual accommodations and clear accessibility guidance (contact recruiting@redwood.ai).

5) New hire onboarding checklist (Day 0–90)

Pre-boarding (before Day 1):
- Recruiting sends offer packet and legal forms via Rippling.
- IT/Systems provisions access: Okta, Slack, Confluence, GitHub, internal services (request via onboarding form).
- Manager shares welcome note, first-week schedule, and 30/60/90 objectives.

Day 0 / Week 1 (Goal: reduce first-week friction):
- HR orientation (benefits, payroll, policies) — scheduled Day 1
- Manager 1:1: role expectations and success criteria
- Team intro & systems walkthrough (codebase, infra, service map)
- Security & compliance training (required within first 5 business days)
- Equipment check (hardware, VPN access, peripheral testing)

30-day checklist:
- Complete onboarding tasks in the tracker
- First deliverable: small scoped task with mentor support
- 30-day manager check-in documented in Confluence (template below)

60-day checklist: 
- Ownership over a recurring task or feature area
- Cross-team introductions completed
- Career development interests capture

90-day checklist (Goal: independent contributor ramp):
- Deliver a project milestone end-to-end
- Performance checkpoint: manager documents progress and calibration notes
- If on track, move to standard performance cadence; if not, create a focused development plan

Onboarding templates (links & text snippets)
- 30/60/90 check-in template: "Accomplishments, Roadblocks, Next Objectives, Support Needed"
- Manager welcome email template (short, includes logistics and day-1 schedule)

6) Performance & feedback cadence

Overview: Redwood uses quarterly performance cycles for calibration, with ongoing feedback and twice-yearly formal reviews for ICs (mid-year and end-of-year). People Ops maintains cycle calendar and calibration norms.

Regular cadence (recommended):
- Weekly 1:1s: manager & report (documented notes and action items)
- Monthly 1:many syncs: team status and cross-team coordination
- Quarterly check-ins: written self-assessment + manager assessment
- Formal review cycles: mid-year (June) and end-of-year (December) for compensation & leveling considerations

Performance calibration & rubric: (table style)
| Area | Expectation | Evidence | Owner |
| Communication | Clear, timely updates; cross-team collaboration | Meeting notes, PRs, incident blameless writeups | Manager |
| Technical impact | Delivers production features and improves metrics | Deployed PRs, dashboards, performance improvements | Manager/IC |
| Ownership | Takes end-to-end responsibility | Roadmap items closed, stakeholder updates | Manager |

Ratings guidance: use a 5-point scale with narrative justification. Avoid forced distribution; focus calibration on impact and evidence. Managers must document examples for ratings of "exceeds" or "needs improvement."

Performance improvement plans (PIP):
- Triggered for sustained performance concerns after documented coaching.
- PIP is a 60- to 90-day plan with clear objectives, measurable success criteria, and weekly check-ins. People Ops must review and approve PIP language before issuance.

7) Manager responsibilities & templates

Hiring:
- Write clear role briefs and scorecards.
- Interview and document scorecards on time.
- Lead debriefs and make final hiring recommendations.

Onboarding:
- Prepare a 30/60/90 plan and share Day 0.
- Assign a mentor within the first week.
- Provide weekly 1:1s and ensure training completion.

Performance & coaching: 
- Conduct weekly 1:1s and maintain notes.
- Provide timely feedback (within 5 business days of observed behavior).
- Document performance conversations and escalate to People Ops for patterns.

Templates (quick-access snippets to copy):
- Manager welcome email: "Welcome [Name]! On Day 1, please join the 9am team standup; I've scheduled 1:1s for the first two weeks. Attached: Day 1 schedule & 30/60/90 template."
- 30-day check-in note (fields): Accomplishments; Areas to improve; Support requested; Next objectives.
- Feedback note template (for Slack/Email): Context -> Behavior -> Impact -> Request for change

8) Systems, tooling, and ownership

Primary systems we use: 
- Greenhouse (ATS & requisitions) — Recruiting ownership
- Rippling (onboard/offboard, payroll) — People Ops ownership
- Okta (SSO & access) — IT/Security ownership
- Confluence (policies & templates) — People Ops owner for HR pages
- Slack (day-to-day comms) — team discretion

Service-level ownership matrix (text table):
| Capability | Owner | SLA 
| Requisition approvals | People Ops | 3 business days for headcount validation 
| Offer drafting | People Ops | 24–48 hours after approval 
| IT provisioning | IT/Security | Completed before Day 1 or escalate within 48 hours 

Escalation paths
- Offer approval delays: escalate to People Ops lead (people-ops-lead@redwood.ai).
- Onboarding provisioning failures: open ticket with IT in the #it-onboarding Slack channel and tag people-ops.
- Performance/legal risks: consult People Ops and Legal before formal steps.

Appendix: Forms & templates (placeholders to copy)
- Role brief checklist: mission, outcomes, required skills, preferred skills, target level, salary band
- Interviewer guide: bias minimization, question examples, timeboxing per interviewer
- PIP template: objectives, success criteria, support offered, review checkpoints

Ownership and governance
- People Ops maintains this playbook and the role band pages.
- Managers and Recruiting must follow these procedures; deviations require written approval from the Head of People.

Change log (sample entries):

Contact & help

- Recruiting: recruiting@redwood.ai
- IT provisioning: #it-onboarding on Slack

This playbook should be reviewed annually or when major process changes occur (e.g., new compensation bands, ATS changes, or legal requirements).
